messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@cardionext.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@cardionext.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: privacy & retention — redlines & pilot conditions

Hi Elena / Tom —

Great to meet yesterday and thanks for the thoughtful questions on data residency and retention. Quick recap from our side plus suggested next steps: 

- CardioNext asks: 0-retention for PII and a 7-day rolling window for non-PII logs; residency in us-west-2.
- What we can commit to today: private deployment (VPC) in us-west-2 is available for Dedicated customers; we can surface a short-term KV cache eviction to limit long-term storage of model context.
- Open items: legal redlines to the DPA (you sent a redline) and an architecture review from Product Ops to confirm the 0-retention flow for PII without breaking debugging/observability.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa / Aditya — can you review the attached DPA redline and SOC2 summary and flag any commercial/legal blockers?
2) CardioNext team — if you can share two short examples of the PII fields you want excluded we’ll validate the redact/zero-retention path.
3) I’ll coordinate a 30-min technical follow-up with our Product Ops to go over logging controls and the canary pilot scope (target next Tue).

If that works I’ll send a poll for the follow-up. Thanks again — we’re excited to make the pilot low-friction.

Best,
Rishi
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment stubs: CardioNext_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (1 page redline), SOC2_summary.pdf (2 pages)
From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@cardionext.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@cardionext.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy & retention — redlines & pilot conditions

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the quick recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) 0-retention for PII is a hard requirement from our privacy team for the pilot (names, national IDs, and account numbers). We need to ensure no PII is persisted beyond request processing.
2) For non-PII telemetry (latency, token counts, anonymized hashes) we can accept a 7-day rolling window.
3) Residency in us-west-2 is required for data-in-flight and log storage for the pilot.

I’ve attached the redline we shared internally — the key legal asks are inline. If Redwood can accept the 0-retention carveout in the DPA scoped to the pilot, we can move straight to a 6-week pilot with a single non-prod model endpoint.

Can Marissa/Aditya call out if there are any concerns on your side, otherwise let’s get the tech session scheduled.

Best,
Elena
Head of Data Privacy | CardioNext
elena.garcia@cardionext.com

Attachment: CardioNext_DPA_redline_v1.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: privacy & retention — redlines & pilot conditions

Rishi — forwarding Elena’s note. Quick internal read: 

- Legal: DPA redline contains a few commercial asks (indemnity language + SLA carveouts) that Legal will want to negotiate. I’ll loop Sarah from Legal if you want me to (I suggest yes).
- Product Ops: 0-retention for PII at the service boundary is doable but depends on how CardioNext wants to supply PII flags. Options:
  a) Client-side markers: CardioNext flags fields as PII in the request (fast to iterate, relies on client accuracy).
  b) Token-level client hashing + server-side redaction rules: slower but centralized.
  c) Zeroing KV-cache + ephemeral logs via a short TTL + immediate forward-only telemetry for metrics.

Ask from Product Ops: need two sample payloads and a list of PII fields to validate the zero-retention flow. Also need a confirmation on whether debug traces for failed requests may contain redacted snippets (we can scrub, but may need limited access for triage).

I’ll start a Legal thread and cc Sarah; Aditya can you schedule the Product Ops call?

-Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Thanks all — putting calendar invites on behalf of Redwood:

- Product Ops technical walkthrough (30m) — Thu 2026-10-15 10:00 PT — invite sent to Elena/Tom + Rishi/Marissa/Sarah from Legal. Agenda: sample payload walkthrough, PII field detection, KV cache eviction timing.
- Legal sync (15m) — Fri 2026-10-16 08:30 PT — to triage DPA redlines and align on concession thresholds for pilot.

Elena — two quick asks before the call: could you drop two sample request payloads (sanitized) into the Drive link I shared and confirm the list of fields you consider PII? That will let us validate the redact/zero path ahead of the call.

Thanks — Aditya (Product Ops)

Aditya / Rishi / Marissa — quick update from CardioNext ahead of Thu:

- We uploaded two sanitized payloads to the Drive link and annotated PII fields in the doc.
- The Legal team is OK with a scoped 0-retention pilot if Redwood accepts the DPA carveout limited to the non-prod pilot environment and if debug traces are redacted before leaving the VPC.

We’re happy to proceed with the technical walkthrough and will be prepared to sign a scoped pilot addendum after the legal sync. Thanks for moving fast here.
